_about: Staged Youth Services records, verified 2026-10-16 against each organisation's own site. NOT yet in resources.json. Fold in after the tidy-up merges: re-run the duplicate check, assign ids, add the category, expand one record per council.

record.name: Muslim Youth Helpline
record.description: Free, confidential, faith and culturally sensitive support for young Muslims. Phone, webchat or email — no judgement, and no one is turned away.
record.notes: For young Muslims across the UK, including Scotland. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Webchat runs 4pm–10pm, 365 days a year. Email replies take 1–3 working days. Because of call volume, calls are limited to once per day; a call-back service is available.

review.age: Designed for young people; 'No one is ever turned away'
flags: No fixed upper age limit stated.

record.name: Clan Childlaw
record.description: Free legal information helpline for children and young people under 26, and adults supporting them, about your rights and the law in Scotland.
record.notes: For children and young people under 26 in Scotland. Not an emergency service — the helpline cannot always give urgent legal advice or get you a lawyer straight away.
record.notes_detail: You can also text 0752 756 6682. Free lawyers to represent young people are available in Edinburgh and the Lothians, and Glasgow and the surrounding area.

flags: Spreadsheet placed it under 5 councils only; that is the lawyer-representation area, the helpline has no area limit.
Helpline closed 22 Oct 2026.

record.name: Scottish Child Law Centre
record.description: Free, confidential legal advice on children's rights and Scots law for under-21s, and for family, carers and professionals who support them. Ask by online form.
record.notes: For children and young people under 21 across Scotland. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Legal advice is requested through the enquiry form on their website, which is only open Mon–Fri 9am–4pm. Replies may take a few days.

flags: Only phone is labelled 'Admin Line'.

record.name: Children First Support Line
record.description: Free support line for parents, carers and families in Scotland. Emotional, practical and financial help, or someone to talk to if you're worried about a child.
record.notes: For parents, carers and families in Scotland, not young people themselves. Not an emergency service. If a child is in immediate danger, call 999.
record.notes_detail: Webchat is also available from the support line page.

review.age: Not stated; line is for adults worried about a child
flags: Parent/carer line — no line for young people themselves.
Reception 0131 446 2300 is a switchboard; deliberately not used.

record.name: YoungMinds Parents Helpline
record.description: Free, confidential advice line for parents and carers worried about the mental health of a child or young person aged 25 or under. Phone, webchat or email.
record.notes: For parents and carers across the UK, not young people themselves. Not an emergency service.

review.age: Parents of a child aged 25 or under
flags: YoungMinds runs no line for young people; its young-person pages only signpost others.
Helpline closed 19–23 Oct 2026 per its own notice.

record.name: Glasgow City Youth Health Service
record.description: Confidential health support for young people aged 12–19 in Glasgow, including short-term help with stress, anxiety and low mood. You can refer yourself.
record.notes: For young people aged 12–19 who live in Glasgow City or have a Glasgow GP. Phone to make a referral. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Young people can refer themselves, or be referred by a teacher, school nurse, parent, GP or other organisation — the referral must be discussed with the young person first. Evening clinics run at health centres across Glasgow City.

record.name: Barnardo's Youth Involvement & Family Support Project
record.description: Family support service for children and young people with a range of emotional needs, and their parents, carers and families.
record.notes: For ages 0–21, or 0–26 if care experienced. Office number, not a support line.
record.notes_detail: Based at Westwood Business Centre, 69–71 Aberdalgie Road, Glasgow G34 9HJ.

flags: Page states no area, hours or referral route; Glasgow City inferred from the G34 address only.

record.name: Lifelink Young Person One-to-One Counselling
record.description: One-to-one counselling for young people in some schools and through Glasgow's Youth Health Services. Help with stress, worry, low mood, confidence and more.
record.notes: For young people at schools with Lifelink counselling or using Glasgow's Youth Health Services. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Ask a teacher or guidance teacher whether your school has Lifelink counselling, or complete the referral form on their website (a teacher, parent/carer or professional can do it for you). If your school doesn't have it, call and they will try to give you information about support in your area.

flags: Partly delivered inside Glasgow City Youth Health Service.
Schools 'across Scotland' unnamed — kept to Glasgow City.

record.name: Volunteer Glasgow Young Persons Befriending Service
record.description: Free befriending for young people aged 8–18 in Glasgow who are dealing with difficult circumstances. You are matched with a trained volunteer for weekly activities.
record.notes: For young people aged 8–18 living in Glasgow. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Anyone can make a referral, with the agreement of the young person and their family. Download the referral form from their website, or email or phone and they can send one out. There is no cost to families.

flags: Befriending, not a mental health service.

record.name: RAMH East Renfrewshire Youth Counselling Service (ERYCS)
record.description: Counselling for young people in secondary schools in East Renfrewshire, during the school day, in a confidential room.
record.notes: For secondary school pupils in East Renfrewshire. Referral is through the Healthier Minds website. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: The phone and email are for RAMH's head office in Paisley.

review.age: No formal age range; 'worked with 10 to 18 year olds'
flags: Spreadsheet listed ERYCS under Renfrewshire — wrong council; it is East Renfrewshire only. The two RAMH cells merged into this one record.

record.name: Trust Jack Foundation
record.description: Mental health and suicide prevention charity. Free one-to-one talking therapy and support groups for young people. You can refer yourself if you are 12–18.
record.notes: Self-referral is for 12–18 year olds who are not already getting support from another mental health service; talking therapy is offered up to age 21. Office number, not a support line. Not a crisis service.
record.notes_detail: Fill in the online referral form on their website and they will contact you to book a telephone assessment. Jack's Hub is at 42 King Street, Stonehouse ML9 3EF — groups run in the evenings. You can also call 01698 793980.

flags: Own pages disagree on area: 'all of Lanarkshire' vs 'North and South Lanarkshire, Ayrshire and Glasgow'. Listed under the two Lanarkshires only.

record.name: Rock Trust
record.description: Advice and support from specialist youth workers for young people aged 16–25 who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
record.notes: For young people aged 16–25 in Edinburgh, the Lothians, Fife, Perth and Kinross, and Glasgow. In some areas access is by referral only. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: If no one is available straight away they aim to get back to you within 24 hours. If you have nowhere to stay tonight, contact your council's homelessness team.

flags: Spreadsheet listed Edinburgh only; own site names 7 council areas. Verified by me directly after the batch agent was captcha-blocked.

record.name: Mindspace Young People's Services
record.description: Counselling and a Recovery College for young people in Perth and Kinross. You can register for counselling yourself using the online form on their website.
record.notes: For young people aged 8–18 in Perth and Kinross. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: For counselling enquiries only, call 01738 631639 or email info@mindspacepk.com (Mon–Fri 8.30am–5pm). For the Young People's Recovery College, email ypteam@mindspacepk.com.

flags: Spreadsheet listed it under Aberdeen City — wrong council; it is Perth and Kinross.
Contact page gives two conflicting sets of hours; left blank.

record.name: The Shed Project
record.description: Youth and community centre in Stornoway offering one-to-one mentoring for young people who are struggling with school, at home, or just need someone to talk to.
record.notes: For young people in Stornoway and Lewis. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: You can ask for mentoring yourself through their website, or a parent or guardian can ask for you. Free youth nights and drop-ins for S1–S6 are at 11 Francis Street, Stornoway.

review.age: Not stated for mentoring; youth nights S1-S6
flags: Mainly a youth club; support element is the mentoring.
Serves Stornoway/Lewis, not all of the Western Isles.
Site shows two postcodes (HS1 2ND / HS1 2NB).

record.name: Youth Enquiry Service (YES)
record.description: Dumfries and Galloway's youth information and support hub. Chat online to a youth worker about anything on your mind, 7 days a week.
record.opening_times: Blether live chat: Mon and Fri 5pm–6pm, Tue–Thu 7pm–8pm, Sat–Sun 12pm–1pm
record.notes: For young people in Dumfries and Galloway. Office number, not a support line. Not a crisis service.
record.notes_detail: Use Blether live chat on their website. In secondary schools, you can refer yourself for one-to-one Blether support (S1 and above), or school staff can refer you.

review.age: No overall range; schools P6-S6, 1-2-1 S1+

record.name: CAMHS Dumfries and Galloway
record.description: NHS specialist mental health service for children and young people in Dumfries and Galloway. Accepts referrals from anyone who knows the child or young person, including self-referrals.
record.notes: For children and young people in Dumfries and Galloway. Not an emergency service — they may not be able to respond the same day. If you are feeling distressed and suicidal, call 999 and ask for an ambulance.
record.notes_detail: If you are over 12, you can refer yourself using the self-referral form on their website. If you are under 12, a parent, carer or professional will need to complete the referral with you.

record.name: Space Youth Befriending
record.description: One-to-one befriending for young people aged 5–16 across Edinburgh who are affected by harms from substance use or gambling in their family.
record.notes: Only for young people aged 5–16 affected by a family member's substance use or gambling. Office number, not a support line. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: A volunteer meets you once a week to try new activities and build confidence.

flags: Befriending, narrow eligibility; not a mental health service.

record.name: The Junction
record.description: Free, confidential health and wellbeing support for young people aged 12–21 in North East Edinburgh. Walk in and talk to a worker one-to-one about anything — stress, difficult emotions, drugs, self-harm, or worries about someone else.
record.opening_times: Walk-In Wed 4pm–7pm; Chill and Chat Fri 12.30pm–3.30pm
record.notes: For young people aged 12–21 in North East Edinburgh. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: Drop-ins are at 82–86 Great Junction Street, Edinburgh EH6 5LL. You can come on your own or bring a friend, family member or support worker. You can also call or text 07758 348850.

flags: Linked to homepage, not /drop-in/: that page carries injected spam linking to fake-ID sellers. Worth telling the charity.

record.name: Well Youth (Mind Your Head)
record.description: Free one-to-one support sessions for young people aged 10–25 in Shetland who are struggling with their mental health. Meet anywhere you feel comfortable and get practical support with whatever you are finding hard.
record.notes: For young people aged 10–25 throughout Shetland. Not an emergency service.
record.notes_detail: To sign up, use the contact form on their website, email or phone. You can also get in touch if you are supporting a loved one through a tough time.

flags: Parent org already listed as 'Mind Your Head' (other-mh, Shetland); this is its distinct youth service.
